newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen B shares end up slightly on rebound.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen B shares end up slightly on rebound.

text.p: Shenzhen's foreign currency B share market staged a technical rebound to close marginally higher on Thursday, spurred by bargain-hunting after Wednesday's steep falls, brokers said.
The B share index rallied 0.96 points or 0.68 percent to close at 143.32 on turnover of HK$73 million against Wednesday's HK$56 million.

However, the A share index gave up early gains and shed 1.83 points or 0.44 percent to 412.91 as state banks pulled funds out of the market under order from the central government, brokers said. Turnover shrank to 4.8 billion yuan from 7.2 billion.
Beijing has ordered state banks to unwind their share positions starting from last Friday within ten sessions, in the latest move to cool down the nation's intensely speculative stock markets.
"Banks are retreating from the A share market in which they had previously built heavy positions," an analyst at a foreign brokerage in Shenzhen said.
"This is going to put downward pressure on the market through next week until the sell-off stops," he said.
The B shares did not extend losses because Beijing's recent clampdown was mainly directed against the A share market which had risen much more sharply, brokers said.
Both the A and B share indices ended sharply lower on Wednesday on panic selling fuelled by apprehension over possible further Beijing crackdown measures, brokers said.
"Concerns over possible new measures will prevent strong rises in the near future," an analyst at China Guotai Securities said.
A wait-and-see attitude is likely to dominate the market on Friday, brokers said.
Strings of anti-speculation measures, ranging from a huge 30 billion yuan new share quota for 1997 to the latest ban on banks from entering the equity markets, have dealt heavy blows to investors.
On the B share market, Shenzhen Health Mineral Water was the heaviest gainer with a rise of HK$0.27 or 8.36 percent to HK$3.50.
Tellus Machinery lost 0.58 yuan or 6.05 percent to 9.01 yuan to become the session's weakest performing A share.
